card.hook: Everyone lines up to be photographed in front of the same side of this 25-foot sign, while the other side stands there with no queue at all. Yes, the sign has a back, and it has a very good message.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign, where the phone icon sits on the map. Then step a little to one side, off the central line, and face the sign at an angle so the bulbs and poles fill the foreground.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the most natural look. Go to zoom 0.5x if the plaza is packed or you're close and want the star, poles and sky all in. Zoom 2x helps you crop out other visitors.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the sign, then slide the brightness down a touch so the bulbs keep their colour instead of washing out.
card.best_time: The flashing bulbs and neon look best as the light fades, so aim for late in the day. After dark, switch on night mode and hold your phone steady against your body or a railing.
card.selfie_here: Use the edge of the grass to either side of the sign, away from the central queue, and pose with the sign over your shoulder. Hold the front camera slightly high, try zoom 0.5x to fit more sign in, or walk round the back for a selfie with the "Drive Carefully, Come Back Soon" side, which is rarely crowded.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand roughly 20 feet back on the grass at the edge of the median, to one side, and to crouch low and shoot upward while you stand by the sign. That way the whole sign fits and the people behind you stay out of the picture.
card.rules_and_safety: Use the marked crosswalks and paved walkway, and never stop on Las Vegas Boulevard or cross traffic elsewhere. Don't jump the line or go underneath the sign for a photo. If you're driving, the car park can only be entered from the southbound lanes, so northbound drivers need a U-turn.
card.challenge: Switch on Live Photo and catch the yellow bulbs mid-flash, then see if you can spot all eight points of the red star in the same shot.
card.good_to_know: Designer Betty Willis created the sign for Clark County, and it went up in 1959. It stands in the median of Las Vegas Boulevard South, and some people consider it the southern end of the Strip. Official access with a small car park and paved walkway arrived in 2008, and marked crosswalks in 2015.

card.hook: Here's the thing about Caesars Palace: you can't fit it in one photo. By 2016 it had 3,960 rooms in six towers, so we're starting at a sidewalk corner and letting the Strip do the talking.
card.stand_here: Stand at the corner of Flamingo Road and Las Vegas Boulevard, with the Roman-style gazebo in the far corner out front of the hotel on the Strip sidewalk. The main hotel is about 380 m to the north-west of this point. Face the gazebo and the boulevard, so the hotel's front grounds are behind you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x so the gazebo, the sidewalk and the boulevard all squeeze in. Switch to 1x for a tidier, less stretched look. Use 2x-5x (depending on your phone) for details like statues or the fountains.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the gazebo on one side of the frame and let the pavement lead into the shot.
card.best_time: Pick a quieter time on the pavement if you want a clean frame. Come after dark for the lights and fountains, switch on night mode and hold still. This corner can fall into shade quickly, so brighten the shadows when you edit.
card.selfie_here: Try the staircase just left of the covered outdoor Spanish Steps Bar when you face Las Vegas Blvd from the casino entrance. One blogger found early-morning light and few crowds there, with Caesars behind you. Or line up in front of the headless statue on the Strip sidewalk by the fountains. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and keep the landmark over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Strip sidewalk in front of the fountains, while you stand in front of the headless statue so the fountain and resort fit behind you (check the framing on the spot).
card.rules_and_safety: Ask staff before taking photos in the casino, and keep your phone close to your body on the busy pavement. A third-party guide says selfie sticks aren't allowed at the Colosseum theatre.
card.challenge: Find the headless statue and strike your best emperor pose, because here every guest is a Caesar.
card.good_to_know: Caesars Palace opened in 1966 and was built to make guests feel like emperors. That's why the name has no apostrophe: every guest is a Caesar. Near the entrance there's a 20-foot (6.1 m) statue of Augustus Caesar, and in 1967 the stunt rider Evel Knievel tried to jump the fountains on a motorbike.

card.hook: Picture a giant glowing moon parked next to the Strip, then it blinks and turns into an eyeball. That's the Sphere, and you don't need a ticket to enjoy its outside.
card.stand_here: Head to LINQ Promenade and face the Sphere across Las Vegas Boulevard. You'll get the whole dome with neon signs in front, so it looks like Las Vegas and not just a glowing ball.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the whole dome and the neon signs. If the crowd pushes you close, drop to 0.5x. Try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for a tighter shot of the screen, and keep your arms steady.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the dome in the upper-middle with the neon signs along the bottom, then tap the dome and drag the brightness slider a little darker so the colours stay rich.
card.best_time: Go from sunset to about 9 PM, when the sky still has some colour and the screen looks bright. The display changes through the day and night, so take a few shots and be ready for a different show than the one you hoped for.
card.selfie_here: Try the corner of Sands Avenue and Koval Lane. Stand on the sidewalk facing back west-northwest toward the dome, with palms on either side, then use the front camera at 0.5x so the dome sits over your shoulder. Manhattan Street, just east of the Sphere, is also good for a close selfie with the dome filling the background.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the Las Vegas Boulevard sidewalk in front of the Venetian or Palazzo, facing northeast, while you stand in front of the casino facade with the Sphere rising behind you, and ask them to shoot wide so you and the whole dome fit.
card.rules_and_safety: Cross Las Vegas Boulevard only at the marked crossings, and step aside from the flow of people before you stop to shoot. Selfie sticks are banned for Sphere events, and you need a ticket to go inside.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the dome looks like a moon, then come back later and see if it has turned into something else.
card.good_to_know: The Sphere is 366 feet (112 m) high and 516 feet (157 m) wide. Its outside carries 580,000 sq ft of LED displays, the largest in the world. It opened on 29 September 2023 with a U2 residency, and you can see the lit shell from several miles away.

card.hook: You can spot the Flamingo from across the Strip because it's pink. Very, very pink. The neon sign and the feather-topped corner are the whole reason people stop and point their phones at it.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Strip sidewalk directly across from the Flamingo, in front of Caesars Palace. The hotel is about 170 m to the east of that point, so face east and look across the street.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to see the sign and hotel front as you see them. Try 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the pink sign and feathered corner and leave the traffic out. Use 0.5x only if you want the whole frontage, but the edges stretch and the building looks smaller.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the sign, then drag the brightness slider a little darker so the pink neon keeps its colour instead of turning white.
card.best_time: Go after dusk, when the neon is lit and the sky is darker. Daytime shows the shape of the building, but the sign has much less punch.
card.selfie_here: Head to the Flamingo entrance sign on Las Vegas Boulevard and stand in front of the entrance with the pink neon sign and greenery behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to fit more in, and go after dark so the sign glows over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the sidewalk facing the pink Flamingo sign while you stand in front of the entrance with the sign behind you, ideally early in the morning when it's less crowded.
card.rules_and_safety: The Strip sidewalk is public, but the hotel and its flamingo habitat are on private property and rules may change, so check the official site first. The habitat can be limited or closed on some days. Pavements get busy, so keep your phone in front of you rather than stepping back into people.
card.challenge: Turn on the gridlines and get the sign on an upper third and the feathered corner filling the other side, with no wonky tower in sight.
card.good_to_know: The Flamingo opened its casino on 26 December 1946 and is the oldest continuously operating resort on the Strip. The original three-storey hotel was demolished in 1993, and today's building is a 28-storey tower with 3,460 rooms. Part of the grounds is a 15-acre pool area with an animal habitat that includes flamingos.

card.hook: Manhattan in Las Vegas, with a rollercoaster looping through it. That's the fun here: a whole skyline squeezed into one long frontage, and something is nearly always moving in your frame.
card.stand_here: Stand at the corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Tropicana Avenue, across the intersection from the hotel's front. Face north-west and the whole casino front fits in one shot.
card.zoom: Start at 1x from the corner to get the full frontage in. Standing closer, on a pavement or the bridge? Switch to 0.5x so the towers don't get chopped off. Use 2x or more (depends on your phone) to pick out the Empire State Building replica or the Statue of Liberty.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the lit towers, then drag the slider to make the picture a touch darker so the lights don't blow out.
card.best_time: Go at night, when the traffic on the boulevard adds streaks of light in front of the glowing towers. Switch on night mode and hold your elbows against your body (or lean on something solid) for a second or two.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold your arm out high so the skyline fits over your shoulder. Keep your face to one side so the towers get their moment too.
card.rules_and_safety: The corner and the lawn across from the hotel may be fenced off for building work, so check on site. Have a backup ready: the pedestrian bridge over Las Vegas Boulevard, or the pavement beside Excalibur looking back at the hotel.
card.challenge: Turn on gridlines and see if you can keep every tower perfectly upright, with the coaster zooming through the frame.
card.good_to_know: The Empire State Building replica has 47 storeys and stands 529 feet (161 m) high. When the hotel opened on 3 January 1997, that made it the tallest building in Nevada, until Wynn Las Vegas was finished in 2005. The Statue of Liberty is just one of the smaller landmark replicas around the tower.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Tropicana Avenue, across the intersection from the hotel's front. Face north-west and the whole casino front fits in one shot.

card.hook: Picture a gold lion the size of a small house, with one of the biggest hotels on the Strip stretching out behind him and taxis streaming past. That's the MGM Grand from the street, and it all fits in one frame.
card.stand_here: Stand at the sidewalk corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Tropicana Avenue, across the intersection from the lion. Face the hotel, which sits to the north-east, with the lion in front and the Strip running behind him.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the lion and the whole hotel front into one frame. Then try 1x for a more natural look, and 2x or higher (depends on your phone) for a close-up of the lion's face.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines and keep your phone level, so the tall hotel stands straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Early or late in the day usually means fewer people on the pavement. After dark, the Strip lights add colour to the background, so let night mode do its thing and hold still until it finishes.
card.selfie_here: Head to Leo the Lion at the MGM Grand main entrance and stand in front of the bronze lion on his pedestal, just as you walk in from Las Vegas Boulevard. Use the front camera, try 0.5x if your phone has it, and keep Leo over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: Pavements here can get busy, so wait for a gap in the crowd before you take the shot.
card.challenge: Get the lion, the full hotel and one passing taxi in the same frame, and see how many tries it takes you.
card.good_to_know: The MGM Grand opened on 18 December 1993. With more than 5,000 rooms, it was the largest hotel in the world at that time. Its first theme was The Wizard of Oz, but most of that went in a big renovation that began in 1996.

card.hook: Picture a footbridge humming above the Strip, taxis streaming underneath, and two glowing towers waiting at the end of the road. That's the Wynn from up high, and it beats the pavement view by a mile.
card.stand_here: Stand in the middle of Fashion Show Footbridge, the pedestrian bridge over Las Vegas Boulevard that links Fashion Show Mall with the Wynn. Face the resort and let the road lead your eye to the towers.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to catch the road, the bridge and both towers. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to fill the frame with the Wynn and Encore. Save zoom 0.5x for when you want lots of Strip, because it makes the towers look small.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the towers on one of the vertical lines, then tap the lit towers and drag the slider a little darker so the bright lights don't wash out.
card.best_time: Go in the evening or after dark, when the lit-up lettering on the tower and the Strip's lights really show. Use night mode and rest your elbows on the rail to keep things steady.
card.selfie_here: Head into the Wynn atrium and stand on the star on the floor in front of the flower-covered carousel, which bloggers rate as one of the resort's top photo backdrops. Use your front camera (zoom 0.5x if it has it) and let the carousel fill the space behind your shoulder. The tree-lined walkway under the lit trees and hanging floral balls is a pretty second pick.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography isn't allowed inside hotel and resort casinos, so keep your selfies to the lobby and atrium. Some parts of the Wynn are private or for guests only, so be mindful where you shoot. The footbridge is a free public walkway, but check it's open before you go.
card.challenge: Get a shot where the road leads straight to the towers and no taxi blocks the way. Bonus points if you keep the railing out of the picture.
card.good_to_know: The Wynn opened on 28 April 2005 on the site of the old Desert Inn, which dated from 1950. Its 45-storey tower was the tallest building in Nevada when it opened. Sister resort Encore followed in December 2008, right to the north, so the two towers sit together on the skyline.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in the middle of Fashion Show Footbridge, the pedestrian bridge over Las Vegas Boulevard that links Fashion Show Mall with the Wynn. Face the resort and let the road lead your eye to the towers.

card.hook: Here's a fun fact to start: only one leg of this Eiffel Tower stands out on the pavement, and the other three are tucked inside a casino. It's half-size, 540 feet (about 165 m) tall, and it still looks very good from across the road.
card.stand_here: Head for the pavement of Las Vegas Boulevard directly across the Strip from Paris Las Vegas, on the Bellagio side. Face the tower, with the Bellagio lake and fountains in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the tower, the facade and the fountain lake in one frame. Then try 1x for a tidier view, and 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the tower top or the big balloon sign.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines, put the tower on a vertical line so it stands straight, and keep the lake along the bottom third.
card.best_time: Day and night both work, so come back once the lights are on. The fountain show runs to a schedule that changes by day, so check times before you go. At night, let night mode finish and keep your phone steady until it's done.
card.selfie_here: Try the sidewalk to the left of the Bellagio fountains, just past the parking entrances. Use the front camera at 0.5x and line up the fountains with the Eiffel Tower replica behind you, over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to crouch by the Eiffel Tower entrance next to Mon Ami Gabi and tilt the phone up, so the whole tower rises behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Stay on legal sidewalks and public walkways, and don't stop in traffic lanes or driveways for a photo (Bellagio Drive is an active driveway). Photos from the Strip are fine, but they're not allowed inside the casinos. The tower's exterior and the light show are free, while the observation deck costs extra.
card.challenge: Hold your phone steady and take a Live Photo of the fountains in motion with the tower standing tall behind them.
card.good_to_know: Paris Las Vegas opened on 1 September 1999 and stands on 24 acres. Behind the tower, the facade has copies of the Arc de Triomphe (two-thirds scale), the Louvre, the Paris Opera House and the Musée d'Orsay. Dave Suder, who worked on the facade, said the buildings were stylised and resized to fit the site, which is why the group looks so tidy in a photo.

card.hook: Picture a skinny concrete needle with a flying saucer on top, sticking up out of a low, squat resort with nothing else around to compete. That's The Strat, and it's tall enough that you'll be steering by it long before you arrive.

card.good_to_know: The Strat opened in 1996 as the Stratosphere and took its current name in January 2020. At 1,149 feet (350 m), it's the tallest observation tower in the United States. Bob Stupak first planned it as a giant neon sign for his Vegas World casino, and the aviation authorities objected to the taller versions he proposed.

card.stand_here: Head for the west sidewalk of Las Vegas Boulevard, in the middle of the Bellagio frontage, and squeeze up to the lake's railing. Face the lake with the Bellagio facade behind the water, and the fountains spread out in front of you to the west.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole lake and the hotel in one shot. Then try 1x for a tidier, less stretched look. Zoom 2x to 5x (depends on your phone) is great for single jets and the sparkly lights on the water.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines to keep the lake edge level, then tap a bright jet and slide it a touch darker so the lights don't wash out.
card.best_time: Go for the first show after sunset, when the sky is still blue and the lights are fully on. Shows usually run every half hour from the afternoon until midnight (more often after dusk), but times change with the season. Get there early, because the railing fills up fast, especially on weekend evenings.
card.selfie_here: Try the railing at the south end of the lake, closer to the Cosmopolitan. Use the front camera at 0.5x, stand in front, and the diagonal angle lets the whole fountain field spread out over your shoulder. The Spago patio inside the Bellagio puts you right in the middle of the lake view, but you'll need a dinner reservation.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone on the pedestrian bridge over Las Vegas Boulevard to aim down at you while you stand by the lake, and check on the map that they can see you.
card.rules_and_safety: Selfie sticks aren't allowed at the Bellagio light shows because they block walking paths, so use your hand. The show is watched from the public sidewalk, and it can be cancelled in strong wind, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Catch the tallest jet at its peak right behind your head, and see how many tries it takes before everyone behind you gets bored of waiting.
card.good_to_know: The show runs on an 8.5-acre man-made lake and is lit by 4,792 white lights. It opened with the resort on 15 October 1998, on the site of the old Dunes hotel-casino. It's often described as one of the most photographed places in the United States.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the west sidewalk of Las Vegas Boulevard, in the middle of the Bellagio frontage, and squeeze up to the lake's railing. Face the lake with the Bellagio facade behind the water, and the fountains spread out in front of you to the west.

card.hook: Picture a neon martini glass on one side, a red Silver Slipper sign on the other, and you standing smack in the middle of the junction like the star of your own casino ad. Fremont Street packs everything close together, so even a quick snap looks like a postcard.
card.stand_here: Stand at the corner of Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard, on the diagonal crosswalk in the middle of the junction, and face the Fremont East sign, the vintage neon martini glass and the red Silver Slipper sign around you. The main canopy is north-west, about 350 m on foot along the pedestrian mall.
card.zoom: At the crosswalk, stay on zoom 1x for the signs and the person in the junction. Once you're under the canopy, switch to zoom 0.5x to fit the arch and the casino fronts into one frame.
card.make_it_pop: Tap a bright sign, then slide the brightness down a little so the neon colours stay rich instead of washing out.
card.best_time: Go after dark, when the neon and the canopy lights are at their best. Weekend nights get very crowded, so aim for earlier in the evening if you want more space.
card.selfie_here: Walk under the canopy on the pedestrian mall, use the front camera at zoom 0.5x and let the lit screen glow above your head. For a higher view, the top level of the Binion's parking garage lets you face away from the Fremont Street marquee so it sits behind you.
card.ask_someone: Hand your phone to a passer-by and ask them to stand well back so the whole sign fits in the frame, with you in the middle of the junction once the signal allows.
card.rules_and_safety: Only step onto the crosswalk when the signal allows. Check the official site for show times and current photo rules, and see whether the Binion's garage top level is open before you head up.
card.challenge: Can you get the martini glass and the Silver Slipper sign on either side of you, with your friend's head exactly on a gridline?
card.good_to_know: The canopy is about 27 m high at the peak and runs four blocks, roughly 419 m, with a giant LED screen on its underside. The light show opened in December 1995, and a 2004 upgrade brought in a 12.5-million-LED display. Before each show, the lights on the buildings underneath are switched off so the screen takes over the street.

card.hook: Walk away from the neon casinos on Fremont Street and you hit a calm, stone-faced 1933 courthouse that looks like it has never heard of a buffet. That contrast is your 'old Las Vegas' photo.
card.stand_here: Stand on the pavement outside the Mob Museum on Stewart Avenue, two blocks north of Fremont Street in Downtown Las Vegas. Face the big old courthouse and step back along the pavement until the whole frontage fits.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for a natural view of the whole building. If the pavement is too narrow to step back, try zoom 0.5x. Then use zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the doorway and stonework.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the building's vertical edges up with them so the walls don't lean, then tap the building and slide it a little darker if the sky is washing out the stone.
card.best_time: Daytime gives clear, even light on the frontage. Early evening adds the glow of street lights and signs, and night mode handles that well if you rest your phone against a post or wall.
card.selfie_here: Try the main entrance at 300 Stewart Ave, with the palm trees that flank the doorway behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone offers it, and hold the phone a little low so the building towers over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: No flash at the museum, and keep clear of exhibits, entrances, exits and busy areas when you shoot. Photo rules inside can vary from room to room, so ask staff first. Personal photos aren't allowed in the third-floor line-up when a museum photographer is there.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole frontage, then one close-up of a detail, and see if a friend can guess where on the building it is.
card.good_to_know: The building was the Las Vegas Post Office and Courthouse, built in 1933, and it's on the National Register of Historic Places. The Mob Museum opened here on 14 February 2012. Inside, the second-floor courtroom hosted one of the fourteen national Kefauver Committee hearings on organised crime, and the museum also displays the brick wall from the Saint Valentine's Day Massacre.

card.hook: A motel lobby shaped like a giant seashell greets you at the Neon Museum, and behind it a gravel path is lined with retired casino signs leaning in like they're gossiping. You get two very different photos in one visit, so grab both.
card.stand_here: Stand at the La Concha Motel lobby and keep a little distance, so the whole sweep of the curved roof fits in your shot. Face the building; the main sign yard is about 3 minutes on foot to the north-west.
card.zoom: Use zoom 0.5x to fit the whole lobby roof in. Switch to 1x for the sign-filled walkway, then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out one sign's lettering without leaning over the barriers.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and line the lobby's edges up with them so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: The lobby looks lovely in soft daylight, and the Neon Boneyard is at its best around dusk, when lit and unlit signs sit side by side. Evening visits are ticketed too, so check the official site for current times.
card.selfie_here: In the Neon Boneyard, stand a few steps in front of the Stardust sign so its starburst fills the frame behind you. For a different look, stand slightly off-centre in front of the Flame sign, where the arrow adds a strong shape behind you. Use the front camera, and try 0.5x if your phone has it.
card.ask_someone: Ask your helper to step back farther from the Stardust sign than feels necessary, while you stand a few steps in front of it, so the whole sign and you both fit in.
card.rules_and_safety: Only phone snapshots are allowed with regular admission. Don't touch, lean on or sit on any sign, stay at least 2 feet away from them, and don't stand on benches or step over the stanchion or rock borders. Large bags and backpacks must be left at security.
card.challenge: Find a single sign against a clear patch of sky and make it look like it's the only star in Las Vegas.
card.good_to_know: The La Concha lobby was donated to the museum in 2005, cut into eight pieces and moved about 3.5 miles north from the Strip in 2006. It's now the visitor centre. The museum opened to the public on 27 October 2012 and now has more than 200 signs.

card.hook: Picture a wheel so big you could lose a whole city block inside its rim, and it still fits in your phone photo. The High Roller does that, and it looks best once the sky goes dark and the lights come on.
card.stand_here: Stand on the LINQ Promenade at ground level near the wheel's base, between the Flamingo and The LINQ. Face the wheel and let the rim and spokes fill your screen.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x, or 0.5x if you want the whole rim in. Standing right at the base, 0.5x lets you look straight up at the spokes. Zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) picks out a few cabins against the sky.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the wheel, then drag the brightness slider down a little so the LED colours stay rich instead of burning out to white.
card.best_time: Go from sunset through blue hour, when the LED colours switch on. One guide suggests about 6-8pm. Check the wheel's hours on the day.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the LINQ Promenade walkway near the High Roller base, with the wheel at the far end of the promenade behind you. Use your front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and keep the wheel over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand behind the In-N-Out on the LINQ Promenade, out of the main walking lane, while you stand with the wheel behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The LINQ Promenade is an open public walkway, but riding the wheel is ticketed. One visitor guide says selfie sticks are encouraged inside the pods, but that's not an official ride rule, so check before you go.
card.challenge: Take three frames a minute or so apart and see if you can catch the wheel in three different colours.
card.good_to_know: The High Roller stands 167.6 metres tall and opened in March 2014 as the world's tallest Ferris wheel. Since October 2021 it has been second tallest, behind Ain Dubai. It has 28 cabins that each hold up to 40 people, and about 2,000 LEDs light it after dark.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the LINQ Promenade at ground level near the wheel's base, between the Flamingo and The LINQ. Face the wheel and let the rim and spokes fill your screen.

card.hook: You're standing on a busy Fremont Street pavement, neck bent back, staring up at a 40-foot neon cowboy who's been grinning down at crowds since 1951. Yes, you'll look like a tourist. That's the idea.
card.stand_here: Stand right beneath Vegas Vic at 25 E Fremont Street, on the Fremont Street side at the corner of First Street, where the phone icon sits. Face the sign and tilt your phone up so he towers over you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x when you're right under him, because it squeezes in the whole figure and some of the canopy. From across the street, use zoom 1x for the whole scene, or zoom 2x to 5x to pick out his face and hat.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the bright neon on your screen, then slide it a little darker so the colours stay rich instead of fading to white.
card.best_time: Neon looks its best once the sky has darkened, so dusk or after dark should suit him well. He's fine by day too, but the glow is less striking.
card.selfie_here: Get your selfie on the pavement right beside Vegas Vic at 25 E Fremont Street, on the corner of First Street. Use the front camera at 0.5x, hold it low and tilt it up so he fits in beside you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand across Fremont Street from the sign, while you stand on the pavement below him, so the whole figure fits in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Don't back up while looking at your screen, and take care around traffic and stairs. The sign is visible from the public street, but check the official site before you go for any events or restrictions.
card.challenge: Find the spot where his hat brim looks a bit trimmed, then frame him so the canopy edge sits just above it.
card.good_to_know: Vegas Vic was put up in 1951 as a friendly, welcoming figure rather than a plain lettered sign. His hat brim lost several feet in 1994 so he'd fit under the Fremont Street Experience canopy, and his red and yellow checked shirt dates from a 1998 restoration. He was refurbished and lit up again in 2023, but he no longer waves or talks.
